newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INTERVIEW-Brazil states start paying their debts.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Brazil states start paying their debts.

text.p: The Brazilian government has started refinancing the debts of the states to halt debt-growth in its stride, and perhaps more importantly, to make the states pay their interest bills, a senior official said Monday.

Pedro Parente, executive secretary of the Finance Ministry, said last week's deal with the southern state of Rio Grande do Sul, in which the government refinanced 6.0 billion reais of the state's debt, will be just the first of several.

The substitution of old short-term debt paying unbearably high interest rates with long-term federal paper paying just 6.0 percent a year, adjusted for inflation, will not only allow interest to be paid -- finally.
But it also involves a commitment by the states to retire about 20 percent of their debt stockpile through asset sales and privatizations.

"This debt swap idea is extremely important," Parente told Reuters. "The objective is to establish a mechanism whereby the states will finally start paying off the principle and the interest on their debts, which hasn't been happening.
"It also provides a stimulus to the deregulation of the public sector in that the states commit themselves to retiring about 20 percent of their debt through the sale of privatizable assets,"
The Rio Grande do Sul deal signed last Friday involves some 6.0 billion reais in debt.

Parente said the Finance Ministry was finalizing details of an accord with Minas Gerais involving 8.0 billion-9.0 billion reais. The figure could vary because Minas has been given permission to issue a global bond to pay off some of its debt.
Rio de Janeiro state was likely to be the next customer after Minas Gerais, followed by Mato Grosso do Sul.
Parente could not give figures for either though news reports have put Rio's debt at 5.0 billion reais and Mato Grosso do Sul's at 2.2 billion reais.
The Finance Ministry official said talks with those states are going well but that negotiations with Sao Paulo were progressing more slowly.

Parente denied that the plan, being billed by newspapers as "the PROER for the states" after the government's special programme to encourage mergers in the banking sector, could involve all the 92 billion reais in debt held by the states.
"It will never reach that. We won't renegotiate debt that has already been refinanced," he said.
He added that it did not represent an increase in total net public sector indebtedness because most of the debt was already backed by government notes.
"In practice, a lot of the states' debts have been guaranteed by federal papers. Now we have a contract with the states whereas before we did not," he said.
According to Central Bank figures, the total net debt of the states and municipalities stood at 81.573 billion reais in June, up from 79.978 billion reais in May.
